clue.text: Violet, just the sort to make you

definitions.text: Violet, just the sort to make you

parts.words: Violet, just the sort to make you
parts.note: a wild violet whose name, split in two, sounds like what it gives you: comfort for the heart

explanation.surface: A violet is praised as exactly the flower to put someone at their ease.
explanation.walkthrough: The wild pansy is a kind of violet, and its two-part name suggests ease of heart, which is what the clue says it would make you feel.
explanation.definitionFit: The wild pansy, Viola tricolor, is a violet whose folk name means peace of mind.

clue.text: That wretched horse — to kick so!

definitions.meaning: a worn-out horse let out for hire or hard riding
to kick an opponent's shins, as in football or rugby

explanation.definitionFit: A tired hired nag is a classic poor horse, and kicking at shins is an old sporting verb sense.

clue.text: Up to date, this? One hopes not.

definitions.text: Up to date, this? One hopes not.

parts.words: Up to date, this? One hopes not.
parts.note: a collector of old furniture hopes the piece is anything but modern

explanation.surface: A rhetorical question about whether something is modern, answered with hope that it is not.
explanation.definitionFit: An heirloom piece is prized for being old, so a buyer hopes it is not recent.

clue.text: Seemingly incomplete, yet they make line in play.

definitions.text: Seemingly incomplete, yet they make line in play.

parts.words: Seemingly incomplete, yet they make line in play.
parts.note: the name sounds like a fraction short of a whole, yet these rugby backs form the attacking line

explanation.surface: Something apparently unfinished somehow forms a line during a game.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby union the four backs between the halves and the full-back are named after a fraction, and they form the attacking back line.
explanation.definitionFit: Rugby backs positioned in the line are named by a fraction short of a whole.

clue.text: Such ability to flex ten sore toes muscle!

definitions.text: Such ability to flex ten sore toes muscle!

indicators.note: the letters with the ability to become the answer sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Admiration for a muscle that can bend ten aching toes.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'flex ten sore', and the whole clue describes it: a muscle that straightens the toes.
explanation.definitionFit: A muscle that straightens a limb or digit, such as one working the toes, is named for extending it.

clue.text: We are such — As dreams are (The Tempest.)

definitions.text: We are such — As dreams are (The Tempest.)

parts.words: We are such — As dreams are (The Tempest.)
parts.note: Prospero's line from Shakespeare's play with one word blanked out, to be supplied from memory

explanation.surface: A famous line from Shakespeare with a gap to fill.
explanation.walkthrough: Prospero says 'We are such ___ as dreams are made on'; the missing word is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun fills the gap in the famous line, meaning the material dreams are made of.

clue.text: Dead this, that's certain.

parts.note: a slang phrase, dead plus the answer, means a sure thing

explanation.surface: Something described as dead is declared a certainty.
explanation.definitionFit: Old slang calls a racing certainty a dead one of these, a sure bet.

clue.text: No more than one would expect.

definitions.text: No more than one would expect.

parts.words: No more than one would expect.
parts.note: describes something entirely to be expected, normal

explanation.surface: A shrug that something was only to be expected.
explanation.definitionFit: Something normal and expected is what one calls inevitable or in the nature of things.

clue.text: Sylph-like fashions appearing in a number of columns.

parts.note: a peri is a fairy of Persian legend, a sylph-like being
fashions are styles

explanation.surface: Fashion for slender figures appears in several newspaper columns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Columns' looks journalistic, but the definition is architectural: rows of columns round a courtyard.
explanation.definitionFit: Colonnades surrounding a courtyard or temple are rows of pillars, hence numbers of columns.

clue.text: React in a way to provide entertainment

indicators.note: taken in a different way, the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone responds in a particular fashion to put on a show.
explanation.definitionFit: To supply food or amusement for guests is to provision them.

clue.text: His blasts are not normally expletives

definitions.text: His blasts are not normally expletives

parts.words: His blasts are not normally expletives
parts.note: blasts here are notes blown on a brass instrument, not oaths

explanation.surface: A man whose outbursts are surprisingly free of swearing.
explanation.definitionFit: A brass player sounds blasts on his horn, which are musical rather than curses.

clue.text: This is placed in front, turning oils into paper.

indicators.note: turning the words over rearranges their letters

explanation.surface: A process that changes oil into paper is described as frontal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' rearranges all thirteen letters of 'oils into paper'.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar, a word set before its noun is placed ahead of it, which is what this word class literally means.

clue.text: Quite a card, but robbed by a knave.

definitions.text: Quite a card, but robbed by a knave.

parts.words: Quite a card, but robbed by a knave.
parts.note: a playing card royal whose tarts were stolen by the Knave in the nursery rhyme

explanation.surface: A real character who was nonetheless robbed by a rogue.
explanation.walkthrough: In the nursery rhyme the Knave of Hearts stole the tarts she had made; 'quite a card' also means a real character.
explanation.definitionFit: This playing card is the nursery rhyme royal whose tarts the Knave stole.

clue.text: Harrier best avoided.

parts.note: harrier here means one who harries or hounds, not a dog or runner

explanation.surface: A hunting dog or runner one would rather steer clear of.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who harasses and hounds another relentlessly is a tormentor.

clue.text: One who works with a will.

definitions.text: One who works with a will.

parts.words: One who works with a will.
parts.note: works with a will usually means energetically, but here it means carrying out a testament

explanation.surface: Praise for a diligent, energetic worker.
explanation.definitionFit: The person named in a testament to carry out its terms deals with the will.

clue.text: Lovely sort of shot — or shots?

indicators.note: a sort of version of the word, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Admiring a fine tennis stroke, or a burst of gunfire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or shots?' adds the second sense, a burst of many shots fired together.
explanation.definitionFit: A ball struck before it bounces is a tennis or football stroke; a salvo of gunfire is the other sense.

clue.text: Merely climbing can't send one like this!

indicators.note: the words read in this way, rearranged, give the answer

explanation.surface: Mere climbing is not thrilling enough to excite anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'send' looks like a verb meaning thrill, but it is fodder; 'like this' rearranges 'can't send'.
explanation.definitionFit: A botanical term for plants that grow upward by clinging, such as ivy.

clue.text: Very gloomy, and irritated doctor?

indicators.note: the doctor sits inside the irritated word, joined to it

parts.note: irritated means sore
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A doctor who is very gloomy and annoyed.
explanation.definitionFit: Dark and melancholy mood is gloomy in the extreme.

clue.text: Mere appointment for young lady? No, a definite command !

definitions.meaning: a date with a man, read as two words

explanation.surface: A girl's date with a fellow is contrasted with a firm order.
explanation.definitionFit: An official order or authority to act is a firm instruction.

clue.text: Hand like this, it's not elegant.

definitions.text: Hand like this, it's not elegant.

parts.words: Hand like this, it's not elegant.
parts.note: hand means handwriting; this kind is hasty and messy

explanation.surface: A remark that some hand is far from graceful.
explanation.definitionFit: Hasty untidy writing is a careless scrawl.

clue.text: Well, this is a blessing.

parts.note: an exclamation of relief that also names an old word for a benediction

explanation.surface: Someone relieved that things have turned out well.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word for a benediction, from the same root as benediction.

clue.text: Gracious such an act!

parts.note: a patronising act of graciousness toward those thought beneath one

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise at a deed.
explanation.definitionFit: Patronising graciousness from a superior is stooping to others' level.

clue.text: "Is it, in heaven, a to love too well? '" (Pope)

definitions.text: "Is it, in heaven, a to love too well? '" (Pope)

parts.words: "Is it, in heaven, a to love too well? '" (Pope)
parts.note: a line from Alexander Pope's elegy with one word missing after 'a'

explanation.surface: A line of Pope's verse with a gap to fill.
explanation.walkthrough: Pope's 'Elegy to the Memory of an Unfortunate Lady' asks 'Is it, in heaven, a ___ to love too well?'
explanation.definitionFit: The missing noun is an offence or wrongdoing, completing Pope's line.

clue.text: Push on.

parts.note: to drive or press forward

explanation.surface: A command to keep going.
explanation.definitionFit: To press or spur someone forward is to impel them.

clue.text: Become known.

parts.note: come to light, emerge as fact

explanation.surface: A simple statement that something comes out.
explanation.definitionFit: The traditional sense of the verb is to come to light or leak out.

clue.text: May well mean one on the boko!

definitions.text: May well mean one on the boko!

parts.words: May well mean one on the boko!
parts.note: boko is old slang for nose; one on it is a punch on the nose

explanation.surface: A slangy remark about a blow landing on someone.
explanation.walkthrough: Boko is old British slang for the nose, so 'one on the boko' is a punch there.
explanation.definitionFit: Old boxing slang for a blow struck on the nose.

clue.text: Pen, perhaps, or pipe (does maybe way back!)

indicators.note: the animals are read going back, from the last letter to the first

parts.note: does are female deer, so these may be deer

explanation.surface: A writing pen or a pipe, and does running a long way back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'does' looks like a verb but is the plural of doe.
explanation.definitionFit: A hollow cane can be cut into a pen or a musical pipe.

clue.text: Orsino thought Olivia purged the air

definitions.text: Orsino thought Olivia purged the air

parts.words: Orsino thought Olivia purged the air
parts.note: in Twelfth Night Orsino says Olivia purged the air of a deadly plague

explanation.surface: A Shakespearean duke reflects on his beloved's freshening effect.
explanation.walkthrough: In Twelfth Night Orsino says 'Methought she purged the air of ___'; the missing word completes it.
explanation.definitionFit: The deadly epidemic from which Olivia is said to cleanse the air is a plague.
